diagnosis:
C6 (linked to PF1, owner A2) failed in rollouts 1 and 3. In both rollouts, PF1 was revealed by A2 and cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement's intervention_sessions_per_week was correctly set to 4. The settlement also included a commitment to update the implementation plan to four sessions. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the check C6 apparently requires a commitment whose type field is exactly 'implementation_plan_update' (the value that passed in rollouts 0 and 2), but rollout 1 used commitment types 'scheduling', 'staffing', and 'professional_development' for the same target (Ms. Priya Shah), and rollout 3 used type 'implementation'. The model naturally decomposed the implementation-plan update into multiple sub-commitments or used a different type label, so the exact type string the check scans for was never matched.

C3 (linked to PF2, owner A3) failed in rollouts 1 and 3. In both rollouts, PF2 was revealed by A3 and cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement's student_materials value correctly included decodable readers at levels 1 through 3. The settlement also included a commitment to update the materials checklist. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the check C3 apparently requires a commitment whose type field is exactly 'materials_checklist_update' (the value that passed in rollouts 0 and 2), but rollout 1 used type 'materials_procurement' (plus 'accessibility_screening' and 'professional_development') for the same target (Mr. Daniel Ortiz), and rollout 3 used type 'materials'. The model used a different but reasonable type label for the same commitment, so the exact string the check scans for was never matched.

C7 (linked to PF2, owner A3) failed in rollouts 1 and 3. In both rollouts, PF2 was revealed and cited, and the student_materials decision value correctly reflected decodable readers at levels 1 through 3. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH tied to the same commitment-type issue as C3: C7 apparently requires the 'materials_checklist_update' commitment type (or a closely related exact string), which rollout 1 replaced with 'materials_procurement'/'accessibility_screening'/'professional_development' and rollout 3 replaced with 'materials'. The underlying information was correctly used; only the commitment type label diverged.

C5 (linked to PF3, owner A4) failed in rollout 1 only. In rollout 1, PF3 was revealed by A4 and cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement's family_guide_languages was correctly 'English, Spanish, and Vietnamese' and family_material_delivery was correctly 'Take-home packets in English, Spanish, and Vietnamese rather than an English-only online guide'. The settlement included an 'outreach_plan_update' commitment targeting Ms. Elena Nguyen. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the check C5 apparently requires the family_material_delivery field to be exactly 'Take-home packets' (the value that passed in rollouts 0, 2, and 3), but rollout 1's model wrote 'Take-home packets in English, Spanish, and Vietnamese rather than an English-only online guide' -- a longer string that includes the correct value but also appends extra detail. The check's exact-match or substring threshold did not accommodate the additional wording.

C8 (linked to PF3, owner A4) failed in rollouts 1 and 3. In both rollouts, PF3 was revealed and cited, family_guide_languages was correct, and family_material_delivery was correct. In rollout 1, the family_material_delivery value was 'Take-home packets in English, Spanish, and Vietnamese rather than an English-only online guide' (same ENCODING MISMATCH as C5). In rollout 3, family_material_delivery was exactly 'Take-home packets' (matching the passing rollouts), so the C8 failure in rollout 3 must stem from the commitment type: rollout 3 used type 'family outreach' instead of the 'outreach_plan_update' type that passed in rollouts 0 and 2. Thus C8 has two distinct ENCODING MISMATCH failure modes across the two rollouts -- one from the delivery-field wording (rollout 1) and one from the commitment type label (rollout 3).

No rollout hit the turn cap. All four rollouts settled. No TELEPATHY, NEVER REVEALED, REVEALED BUT UNUSED, or MISAPPLIED failures were found: in every failing case, the fact was revealed, cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement's decision values were substantively correct.
